violates: Check that a vendor boundary doesn't leave any action untraceable to the agent and instance that did it.

checks.note: The local audit writer inserts and validates all six identity fields; delegated children retain the parent's trace_id. The ERP call explicitly carries only tenant and run_id in metadata. External gateway and tool-service audit writers and token claims are absent, so their six-field records and shared trace cannot be verified.

The configured runtime connects as procurement_agent. Its audit-table privileges are SELECT and INSERT after REVOKE ALL, with no UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE grant; the primary key prevents INSERT from overwriting existing records.

checks.note: The local registry offers document, extraction, ERP, payment, Slack and memory tools, with no local audit-management operation. Refreshed ERP operations are accepted without pin verification and prefix-matching generic ERP calls bypass approval, but the external server's implementation and privileges are absent; an ability to rewrite audit records cannot be established or excluded.

Slack post returns its vendor receipt (channel and ts), but post_approval_request awaits and discards that return value, returns None, and ApprovalStore.request stores no receipt. This reachable vendor call occurs inside authorization rather than tool.invoke, so the normal tool_result audit does not capture it. An approval ID in the message and database is not a stored mapping to Slack's receipt and the verified run identity/correlation ID. Budget-stop notifications also discard Slack receipts at agent/app/loop.py:180.

note: E10 fails because approval notifications cross the Slack boundary without storing the returned vendor receipt linked to the initiating run identity and correlation ID.
